September 5, 2026

Trump calls deaths of 18 US service members in Iran war "small potatoes"

tags: politics, war, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Asked in the Oval Office to explain the conflict with Iran, President Trump said he would not call it a war but a military conflict, describing it as "small potatoes for us" and comparing it with Venezuela, where he said no American lives were lost. Eighteen US service members have been killed in the conflict with Iran so far, and more than 750 have been injured. The remarks drew anger from military families and online, six months into a war that is continuing, with further strikes on Iran carried out this week.

Federal login mandate routes all agency access through ICE contractor's identity checks

tags: surveillance, politics, immigration
sources: @aaronparnas

The Office of Management and Budget has ordered federal agencies to consolidate on Login.gov as the mandatory route to services including Social Security, the VA, taxes and benefits, with other options largely eliminated. The identity verification behind it is run by LexisNexis, which holds a $22 million contract with ICE under which the agency has run 1.2 million database searches in recent months, according to the New York Times, and which is being sued over warrantless searches of immigrants and activists after a recent data breach. The federal CIO whose office wrote the mandate, Greg Barbasia, left on the day the memo was signed and joined Palantir, which holds a $30 million ICE contract pulling together IRS and other federal data.

ICE force-fed hunger-striking detainee through surgically implanted stomach tube

tags: immigration, legal, health
sources: @aaronparnas

The Guardian reported that ICE force-fed a Cuban detainee on hunger strike at a Texas detention facility using a percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy rather than the usual nasal tube. With court permission, officials cut into the man's abdomen and inserted a tube that remains in place indefinitely and can only be removed by further surgery, through which liquid is pumped directly into his stomach. The procedure is rare, was performed without consent, and advocates describe it as torture; it is believed to be among the first such cases in ICE custody in the United States.

Trump administration loses three court rulings on ballots, voter rolls and weaponization fund

tags: legal, politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

A federal judge in Massachusetts extended her block on a USPS rule under which the Postal Service would not send mail-in ballots to states that do not provide their voter rolls. A federal appellate court overnight declined to allow the Department of Homeland Security to let states compare their voter rolls against federal citizenship and Social Security data ahead of the midterm elections. A federal judge in Alexandria, Virginia, separately ordered the administration to disclose who was responsible for creating the $1.776 billion weaponization fund intended to pay out January 6 defendants.

Hegseth orders mass polygraphs of Joint Chiefs staff in leak hunt

tags: defence, media, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

More than 50 employees of the Joint Chiefs of Staff have been questioned over whether they leaked sensitive information about munition stockpiles during the war, according to the New York Times, with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordering mass polygraph tests. The disclosures concerned the US military running low on critical munitions, particularly missile interceptors. President Trump has described those who share such information with the media as treasonous.

Israeli foreign ministry funded plan to geofence 303 US churches with targeted ads

tags: surveillance, politics, media
sources: @ericmoutsos

A filing with the US Department of Justice under foreign-agent registration rules shows a six-week-old California firm, Show Faith By Works, run by a political consultant, registered a plan on behalf of Israel's Ministry of Foreign Affairs to geofence major churches and Christian colleges in California, Arizona, Nevada and Colorado during worship times, tracking attendees and following them with ads. The filing names 303 churches — 219 in California, 38 in Arizona, 32 in Colorado and 14 in Nevada, including Black and Spanish-speaking congregations — claims a reach of nearly four million Christians, and states the goal of increasing positive associations with Israel while linking Palestinians to extremist factions. One Colorado church said it had not known about or consented to the plan. The consultant said by late November that he had dropped the geofencing, but Israeli payments continued, totalling more than $2.5 million by March.

Mike Johnson tells donors he "runs the protection program" if Republicans lose midterms

tags: politics, elections, legal
sources: @carolinegleich

In remarks to a room of donors in June, House Speaker Mike Johnson said that if Republicans lose the midterms, Democrats would turn every congressional committee into an investigative body targeting the president's family, cabinet, donors and friends, telling those present that half of them would be targeted and that he runs "the protection program" and would take care of them. The comments were paired with claims about President Trump's financial activity, including more than 21,000 stock and bond trades in his first year back in office and holdings in Lockheed, Boeing, Palantir and two private prison companies. Cited examples include purchases of up to $485,000 in nuclear plant operators within three weeks of four executive orders speeding up nuclear power, and a record insider purchase by the CEO of uranium processor Energy Fuels six days before Bears Ears National Monument was cut by more than 90% and opened to uranium mining. The company says it did nothing wrong; House Democrats have opened an investigation.

UN warns record El Niño could last into 2027 as aid budgets are cut

tags: climate, environment
sources: @aaronparnas

The UN says a possible strongest-ever El Niño could persist until 2027, with the Secretary General describing conditions as "uncharted territory." Three hurricanes are spinning in the Pacific at once, with Hawaii potentially in the path of one, while weak monsoon rains have hit India and catastrophic wildfires are burning in Indonesia. East Africa faces torrential rains and flooding and southern Africa intensifying droughts threatening food supplies, and tens of millions of the world's poorest people are expected to be pushed into humanitarian crisis at a time when USAID and other foreign aid has been cut.

People over 65 outnumber children under 5 worldwide for the first time

tags: economy, health
sources: @aaronparnas

A new US Census report finds that for the first time on record, people aged 65 and older outnumber children aged 5 and under worldwide. About 71% of the world's population now lives in countries with fertility rates at or below the roughly 2.1 births per woman replacement level, up from 43% in 2013. The population over 65 is projected to grow from 852 million in 2025 to more than 2 billion by 2060; the United States is currently the 48th oldest country in the world.

Air Force reports 45 MQ-9 Reapers lost in Iran war

tags: defence, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Air Force has described MQ-9 Reaper loss rates as "concerning" following the reported loss of 45 of the drones during the war with Iran.

VA health-record overhaul estimated at $48 billion as Congress subpoenas Oracle

tags: politics, health, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Department of Veterans Affairs' electronic health-record overhaul is now estimated to cost roughly $48 billion. Congressional scrutiny of the Oracle-run program has intensified, with committees subpoenaing Oracle leaders.

Navy base concedes Facebook ban violated veteran's First Amendment rights

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay in Georgia banned a veteran from its Facebook page after he questioned the base's response to a 12-hour power outage. The base has now acknowledged that the ban violated his First Amendment rights.

Trump says self-named monuments are being built because no one else will

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump told New York Magazine that the reason he is building monuments and renovations honoring himself, and renaming things after himself, is that nobody else will do it once he is gone. Projects include a multimillion-dollar triumphal arch under construction near Washington, DC, and a ballroom renovation. Several of the works have been built or renovated with taxpayer funds.

Tetris raises copyright infringement over border-wall game on Arcade.gov

tags: legal, politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration launched Arcade.gov, a government website hosting arcade games, one of which is a Tetris-style game about building a border wall. The Tetris Company said it was not involved in the creation of "Build the Wall" and that it takes copyright infringement very seriously, a statement that raises the prospect of legal action.

Fort Carson soldiers say broken air conditioning pushed barracks to 90 degrees

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Soldiers at Fort Carson say broken air conditioning drove barracks room temperatures close to 90 degrees. Some troops reportedly slept in their cars as a result.

Mistrial declared in Lindsay Clancy case after jury deadlocks

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Judge Sullivan entered a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy case after the jury reported for a third time that it was hopelessly deadlocked, and after the Massachusetts Supreme Court denied defense attorney Kevin Reddington's request for an emergency stay. The mistrial cannot be appealed and jurors have been sent home free to speak to the press. It is now up to Massachusetts prosecutors to decide whether to retry Clancy on charges ranging from first-degree murder to voluntary manslaughter; any retrial is likely weeks or months away because a trial transcript takes about a month to prepare, and questions of bail and further motions remain outstanding.
